Changed paths:
- `bin/muse-acp.mjs` — empty assistant replies (Muse busy with native tools) no longer count as blockless, draw no nudge, and don't end the turn: the bridge emits one "Muse is working with its own tools…" thought and polls `driver.history` for a non-empty message; `NUDGE_MESSAGE` now explains muse-tool is a text block, native tools run on the cloud VM, and web results come back via `write_file`; `MUSE_BRIDGE_FAKE_SCRIPT` array elements = one Muse turn whose tail items land in history ~200 ms apart.
- `bridge/acp-pending.mjs` — new `waitForAssistantMessage()`: returns the next finished non-empty assistant message after the last user message; each newly seen message resets the idle clock; `""` on timeout.
- `bridge/acp-tools.mjs` — `buildIntro()` gained the muse-tool-vs-native-tools paragraph (text block run by the BB bridge, native tools on the cloud VM, `write_file` for deliverables, `browser.*` for the web).
- `bridge/acp-prompt.mjs` — every attached file ≤10 MB goes as a real Muse attachment with only `[Attached file: <name> — sent as an attachment]` in the text; >10 MB text inlines truncated, binaries get the not-sent line. Covers `resource_link` and embedded `resource` (text and blob), so the Muse Image path inherits it.
- `tests/native-tools.test.mjs` (new) — late-reply-after-empties, idle-timeout continue hint, non-empty blockless still nudged, intro assertions.
- `tests/acp-attachments.test.mjs`, `tests/attachments-acp.test.mjs` — repinned to attachment semantics (strict asserts kept, incl. >10 MB inline/not-sent cases).
- `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `version.ts` — bumped to **0.3.13**, not 0.3.11: both 0.3.11 (bridge-multi-tool) and 0.3.12 (bridge-nudge) are already merged on main, so the contract's literal version was unsatisfiable and only a forward bump is correct.

Heads-up, outside owns_paths: `tests/ui-panel.test.mjs:81` hard-pins `PLUGIN_VERSION === "0.3.12"` (left by `muse-panel-layout`) — it fails on the full suite with the bump and needs a one-line update on your side. Not in the task's verification commands.

- In verification scripts and tests that create temp dirs, use /tmp explicitly (mktemp -d /tmp/x.XXXXXX, or TMPDIR=/tmp): the writer sandbox denies mkdtemp in the system TMPDIR under /var/folders. Keep PM-written check scripts in /tmp/<name>/ (the guard blocks .mjs under .agents/).
- In a folder without git (live-folder mode), never put a task's expected_outputs or owns_paths under .bb/ (chat folders): the live snapshot skips .bb, so a file written there is never counted as produced and the task blocks as missing expected_outputs. Put task deliverables in a project folder such as docs/ or reports/.
- Правя тестовый файл из owns_paths, меняй только ожидаемые значения внутри существующих строгих assert (deepEqual/equal) и добавляй новые проверки рядом — не удаляй строки assert и не ослабляй строгую проверку до assert.ok/includes/truthiness; перед ответом перечитай свой diff по тестам и верни всё, что стало слабее: test_fit помечает это как сломанную проверку, и попытки сгорают до лимита.
- For a BB ACP provider, check every launch spec and output shape against BB's own bridge code before shipping: permission flags are inserted at permissionCli.insertAfterArgs (default 0, so a /bin/sh -c wrapper needs insertAfterArgs after its args), and agent_message_chunk keeps only text (image blocks are dropped; show pictures as Markdown ![alt](workspace-relative path)).
- In muse-ai-connector, every check script or test that imports bridge/ modules must set MUSE_BRIDGE_HOME to a fresh mkdtemp under /tmp before the import; never let a check write into the real ~/.muse-bridge (accounts, cookies, cache).

{"summary":"This task addresses three interrelated issues in the BB-to-Muse bridge (muse-ai-connector) when Muse executes native cloud tools: handling empty intermediate responses, clarifying the nature of `muse-tool` versus native VM tools in system instructions, and transmitting user-attached files as native Muse attachments rather than inlined text.

1. Native Tool Execution and Empty Replies:
Chat history from 2026-11-03 shows that when Muse runs its native tools (such as `browser.search`, `browser.open`, or `subagent.spawn`), it emits assistant messages containing empty content (`""`) with `streaming: false` while awaiting asynchronous results. In the current implementation of `bin/muse-acp.mjs`, `driver.send()` returns this empty text. `parseToolCalls("")` classifies it as `kind: "none"`, and because `stripDoneMarker("")` is null, the bridge treats it as a blockless reply. It increments `blockless`, transmits `NUDGE_MESSAGE` ("Your last reply had no ```muse-tool block..."), and after `MAX_BLOCKLESS_REPLIES` (3), terminates the BB turn with `BLOCKLESS_STOP_MESSAGE` before Muse ever returns its actual text answer.

The plan specifies that empty or whitespace-only assistant messages must not be treated as answers: they must not increment the blockless counter, must not trigger a nudge, and must not end the turn. Instead, the bridge must continue waiting on the Muse chat for the subsequent non-empty assistant message (polling `driver.history(chatId)` approximately every 3 seconds or resubscribing via the API transport) up to `REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS`. Each received empty message resets the idle timer. During this wait, a single progress update must be streamed to BB (`agent_thought_chunk`: "Muse is working with its own tools…"). If a timeout expires with only empty messages received, the turn must end with an explicit user message ("Muse is still working on its side; ask it to continue") rather than an empty message or abrupt stop. Nudges are reserved strictly for non-empty replies that lack both a tool block and a `[[done]]` marker.

2. Intro & Nudge Clarity:
`buildIntro()` in `bridge/acp-tools.mjs` and `NUDGE_MESSAGE` in `bin/muse-acp.mjs` must be updated to clearly differentiate Muse's cloud execution environment from the local user workspace. Specifically, instructions must state that `muse-tool` is not one of Muse's native tools, but a fenced text block parsed by the local BB bridge to execute operations on the user's machine; that Muse's native tools (`muse.read`, `muse.write`, `muse.exec`, shell) operate solely on its cloud VM and cannot see or modify the local workspace; and that native browser tools should be used for web retrieval followed by `muse-tool write_file` to write files into the workspace.

3. Native File Attachments:
Currently, text files passed via `resource` or `resource_link` are inlined into the prompt text as `[Attached file: <name>] ~~~ <body> ~~~`, while binary files and images are sent as real attachments. Under the new contract, all attached files up to 10 MB must be dispatched as real Muse chat attachments (preserving existing attachment paths), leaving only a single reference line in the prompt body: `[Attached file: <name> — sent as an attachment]`. Files exceeding 10 MB will continue to be inlined with a truncation notice.

4. Verification & Scope:
Acceptance requires running `node /tmp/muse-native/check.mjs <checkout>` (verifying real text attachment routing without inlined body, updated intro text, and waiting through two empty messages without nudging), creating `tests/native-tools.test.mjs` covering idle timeouts and non-empty blockless nudges, bumping the package version to 0.3.11 in `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and `version.ts`, and passing `node --test` across four test suites along with `npm run typecheck`.
